project.name: core-api
project.description:
Service-to-service contract for the core host (V9 §18 / §91).
Members: ModelGateway (the runtime model-routing SPI) and its nested ModelEndpoint record, plus FeatureModelNotConfiguredException, which is the only failure the SPI may raise and which callers in other deployment units are required to propagate rather than swallow. Plus UserLookupPort, the display-name lookup that stops other domains from reading the user table.
Why UserLookupPort is here and not in a hypothetical identity-api. The section 18 module list fixes eight contract names and identity is not one of them; core-api is the contract for the dinqor-core-host deployment unit, which is exactly where identity lives, so the same reasoning that put ModelGateway here applies. Two domains used to inject identity.infrastructure.UserMapper (a MyBatis mapper) and identity.domain.User (the sys_user entity) just to render an author name: publishing.application.BlogService, and components.application.ComponentService. That is what identity's own package-info forbids ("feature modules ... must not parse tokens or query the user table directly"), and for publishing it crossed a deployment unit as well (dinqor-content-automation reaching into dinqor-core-host). The port exposes exactly one method and returns null when it cannot answer, because the two callers have *different* fallbacks ("User {id}" versus "anonymous {id}") and a fallback is display policy, not identity data. Do not widen this port: every method added is another way around the boundary, and widening breaks nothing, so UserLookupPortTest pins the method count.
Why these three and nothing else. ModelGateway is an interface whose *implementation* (ModelGatewayService, reading model_provider / model_feature_config) stays in the admin domain of dinqor-core-host, while its *consumers* sit in three different future deployment units: dinqor-agent (AgentModelClient), dinqor-content-automation (BlogAgentImageClient, BlogAgentModelClient) and dinqor-core-host (DashScopeRecitationAsrClient, Img2ThreeModelClient). An interface owned by the provider but implemented only there, and depended upon across a service boundary, points the wrong way once the split happens; the port moves to a module both sides may depend on. This is the same reasoning as contracts/content-api, and unlike contracts/integration-api it is a pure move: the type was already an interface, so no port had to be invented.
The exception travels with the interface, not with the implementation. FeatureModelNotConfigured is documented behaviour of the SPI ("the gateway is on and this feature has no usable endpoint"), and BlogAgentImageClient catches it and GlobalExceptionHandler maps it to HTTP 400. Leaving it in the admin domain would keep a cross-unit import alive for no benefit.
Zero dependencies, and that is the point. A contract that drags in a framework cannot be depended on by every service, and V9 §19 is explicit that the WebFlux Gateway must stay free of spring-webmvc. Nothing here may gain a compile dependency without a deliberate decision; test scope is fine. Note that ModelEndpoint deliberately exposes the decrypted apiKey as a plain String: this module is about the shape of the value, not about how it is protected. ProviderKeyCipher, the AES key handling and the provider registry all stay in admin.
The package is com.xander.lab.core.api rather than com.xander.lab.core. "core" is not a business domain, but a bare first segment would still be classified as one by the cross-domain scanner, and the contract would then be invisible in the metrics; the dotted entry "core.api" is registered in SHARED_KERNEL for exactly that reason (see docs/migration/lib-extraction.md §6.1).
What is deliberately NOT here: the resolved-endpoint cache, the per-feature assignment rules, the api-style whitelist validation (FeatureModelConfigService) and the admin HTTP surface. Those are behaviour and stay in admin. What IS here is the vocabulary the behaviour speaks: the feature keys and the api styles, which are persisted as model_feature_config column values and therefore cannot be renamed casually.
